workLog.action: Added one always-on rule and moved the semgrep specifics to GOTCHAS
workLog.outcome: Adversarial review recommended cutting the second rule and shortening the first. Both were right. The cut rule was a general debugging heuristic, and its cited evidence was false: I wrote that a sibling pull request modified the same file at the same lines, and the hunk headers show 4723 touching 542, 904, and 928 while 4701 touched 721. I had published an unverified claim inside the rule written to stop me publishing unverified claims. Always-on growth fell from 1267 bytes to 451.

workLog.action: adr-review: multi-agent review of ADR-093, both findings acted on
workLog.outcome: Architect returned accept with one wording change; critic returned revise on two grounds. Both are now addressed. The critic argued the rule would not fire for an agent who believed the tools already matched, which is a fair reading of the original wording, so the rule now requires the equivalence to be demonstrably identical rather than merely matching: belief cannot satisfy a demonstration. The critic also caught that no CI-side fix was evaluated, which was a real gap, and checking it changed the advice: semgrep ci run while logged in executes the rules configured on Semgrep App, so SEMGREP_APP_TOKEN=<token> semgrep ci is an exact reproduction and the check is locally reproducible after all. The GOTCHAS entry claimed the opposite and has been corrected. Always-on growth is now 472 bytes.
